title: Rib Older Than Maps
text: A damaged traveler journal records: The smallest exposed rib is longer than a palace corridor and predates every chart of the Wake.

title: Pressure Language
text: An old field report states: Deep shelters mark danger with dents rather than ink because written signs fracture under the pressure.

title: The Feeding Scar
text: A local record preserves this account: A smooth trench across the seabed records where a leviathan once dragged its jaw through solid stone.

title: Scale-Shelter Rule
text: An unsigned observation reads: Wreck crews survived storms by anchoring beneath shed scales, never beneath bones that might still move.

title: Do Not Knock
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: Shizuki wrote on a colossal tooth: "Something knocked back. We are leaving this mystery unsolved."

title: Specimen Harness
text: An old field report states: A broken restraint is sized for a creature larger than any vessel and bears the organization's later insignia.

title: Wakewatch Log
text: A local record preserves this account: Observers measured current changes days before a leviathan passed, allowing settlements to evacuate without seeing it.

title: Marrowlight Ecology
text: An unsigned observation reads: Small luminous creatures nest in hollow bones and defend them as though the skeleton were alive.

title: The Crushed Fleet
text: A damaged traveler journal records: Seven ships lie compressed into one another, all pointing away from the same unseen source.

title: Research Annotation
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: Shizuki added: "Calling it a controllable asset did not make it controllable. The wall demonstrates this."

title: Pressure Bell
text: A local record preserves this account: A bronze bell rings only when the surrounding water reaches a depth dangerous to unprotected divers.

title: Migration Without Bodies
text: An unsigned observation reads: Currents follow ancient routes even though the leviathans that carved them have vanished.

title: Titan Scale Census
text: A damaged traveler journal records: Each recovered scale carries a different celestial pattern, suggesting the Wake held several distinct species.

title: Weaponization Proposal
text: An old field report states: A damaged proposal recommends directing leviathan movement toward rebellious settlements and rival facilities.

title: Emergency Exit, Enlarged
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: Shizuki's handwriting reads: "I improved the exit after the test subject improved the wall."

title: The Listening Bone
text: An unsigned observation reads: One vertebra amplifies distant songs from far beyond the mapped Wake.

title: Hullsplitter Report
text: A damaged traveler journal records: Salvagers blamed a predator until tooth marks proved the wreck had been bitten after it sank.

title: Sedated Thunder
text: An old field report states: A research log describes a heartbeat heard through three sealed pressure doors.

title: Wakeheart Current
text: A local record preserves this account: The central current accelerates in a rhythm too regular to be explained by tides.

title: Tiny Warning Sign
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: Shizuki attached a miniature sign to an enormous claw: "Danger: very large personal space."

title: Program Designation
text: A damaged traveler journal records: The Behemoth Program inherited staff titles and equipment from several older annex operations.

title: Failed Command Tone
text: An old field report states: Constructs broadcast a control signal that nearby creatures learned to imitate back at them.

title: Ancient Tooth Record
text: A local record preserves this account: Growth bands within the tooth contain traces of regions that no longer exist.

title: The Weapon Refused
text: An unsigned observation reads: A final trial report admits the altered creature ignored its target and destroyed the observation platform instead.

title: Later Correction
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: Shizuki wrote: "It was never their weapon. It was an animal in pain. Write that part larger."

title: Gravewing Route
text: An old field report states: Mantas still avoid the corridor once used to transport restrained leviathan specimens.

title: Artificial Scale
text: A local record preserves this account: One scale is built from layered metal and living coral, with attachment points facing inward.

title: Program Survivors
text: An unsigned observation reads: Personnel records continue across generations, stasis cycles, and replacement bodies without clarifying which method was used.

title: The Empty Holding Sea
text: A damaged traveler journal records: The largest enclosure stands open, its restraints broken outward and its inhabitant unrecorded.

title: A Continuing Wake
text: A page in Shizuki's familiar handwriting says: The final program ledger sends results onward to a central project rather than recording the work as complete.
